q: An instrument used to measure deformation.
n: An extensometer measures deformation (change in length) of a specimen under load. Source: ASTM E83 (Extensometer Systems).

q: Which instrument records ground acceleration during an earthquake?
n: An accelerograph (strong-motion recorder) records ground acceleration during an earthquake. Source: PHIVOLCS; Chopra, Dynamics of Structures.

q: What is a material's resistance to deformation under stress?
n: Stiffness is a material's or member's resistance to deformation under stress. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: Atransformer vault is considered a:
n: A transformer vault is a heavy load at one location, a concentrated load. Source: NSCP 2015, Chapter 2 (concentrated loads).

q: Furniture counts as what kind of load?
n: Furniture is movable contents, so it counts as live load. Live loads are movable and variable, unlike the permanent dead load of the structure. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 205.

q: What is force per unit area?
n: Stress is force per unit area. Stress is measured in Pa, MPa or psi, and its main types are tensile, compressive and shear. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What is the deformation of a body under load?
n: Strain is the deformation of a body under load, change in length over original length. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: A force that pulls an elastic body apart is a:
n: A tensile force pulls an elastic body apart. Tension stretches a member, as in cables, ties and the bottom chord of a truss. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What is the greatest stress a material can take before it fractures?
n: Ultimate strength is the greatest stress a material can take before it fractures. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What is the stress beyond which a material doesn't return to its original length?
n: Beyond the elastic limit a material keeps a permanent set and does not return to its original length. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What is another term for the elastic limit?
n: The elastic limit is commonly equated with the yield point, the stress beyond which deformation becomes permanent. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What is the tendency of a slender member to bow under compression?
n: Buckling is the tendency of a slender member to bow sideways under compression. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: Which property is resistance to indentation or scratching?
n: Hardness is resistance to indentation or scratching. Source: Callister, Materials Science and Engineering.

q: What is a space frame built to carry all vertical gravity loads?
n: A vertical load-carrying space frame is a space frame built to carry all vertical gravity loads. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208 (definitions).

q: What is an element that deforms much more under lateral load than adjoining parts?
n: A flexible element deforms much more under lateral load than adjoining parts of the system. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208 (definitions).

q: Which method distributes total lateral force to vertical elements in proportion to their rigidity, considering the diaphragm?
n: Distribution of horizontal shear allocates the total lateral force to vertical resisting elements in proportion to their rigidity, accounting for the diaphragm. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208.8.3 (horizontal distribution of shear).

q: Anassemblage of framing members designed to support gravity loads and resist lateral forces is called a:
n: A frame is an assemblage of framing members that supports gravity loads and resists lateral forces. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208 (definitions).

q: What is a space frame whose members and joints resist forces mainly by flexure?
n: A moment-resisting space frame resists forces mainly through flexure of its members and rigid joints. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208.4.6.

q: Which ASTM standard covers deformed steel welded wire fabric?
n: ASTM A497 covers deformed steel welded wire reinforcement. A496 covers the deformed wire itself. Source: ASTM A497 (now consolidated in A1064).

q: Which ASTM standard covers deformed and plain carbon-steel bars for concrete?
n: ASTM A615 covers deformed and plain carbon-steel bars for concrete. A706 is low-alloy weldable bar. Source: ASTM A615.

q: Which ASTM standard covers ready-mixed concrete?
n: ASTM C94 covers ready-mixed concrete. C150 covers cement and C143 the slump test. It sets requirements for materials, mixing, delivery and testing of concrete batched at a plant. Source: ASTM C94.

q: Which document is the standard for structural concrete design and construction?
n: ACI 318, Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete, is the standard for structural concrete design and construction. NSCP Chapter 4 is based on it. Source: ACI 318-14; NSCP 2015 Chapter 4.

q: Which ASTM standard covers stainless steel bars and shapes?
n: ASTM A276 covers stainless steel bars and shapes. These alloys contain chromium, which forms a passive layer and gives corrosion resistance. Source: ASTM A276.

q: What is the live load of hardware and tools (in kg/m?)?
n: Heavy storage of hardware and tools calls for a high design live load. The item gives 2,000 kg/m². Actual design should follow NSCP Table 205-1 (heavy storage) or the real stored weights, if higher. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 205-1 (minimum uniform live loads).

q: What is the design load of copper (in kKN/m?)?
n: Copper weighs about 8,900 kg/m³, so its unit weight is 8,900 × 9.81 ≈ 87.3 kN/m³. Source: NSCP 2015, Table 204-2 (material weights); Callister.

q: What do you call the point at which a material is about to rupture?
n: Ultimate strength is the stress at which a material is about to rupture, the peak of its stress–strain curve. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.

q: What is nominal strength times the strength reduction factor φ?
n: Design strength is nominal strength times the strength reduction factor (φRn), which must be at least the required strength Ru. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 421.1.

q: Which SI unit of force is about 0.225 lb?
n: One newton is about 0.2248 lbf, so about 0.225 lb of force. One newton is the force that accelerates 1 kg at 1 m/s². Source: NIST SP 811 (SI units).

q: What stress stays locked in a material from manufacturing?
n: Residual stress stays locked in a material from manufacturing (rolling, welding, uneven cooling). Source: AISC 360 Commentary; Gere & Goodno.

q: At what stress does a material begin to deform permanently?
n: Yield strength is the stress at which a material begins to deform permanently. Source: Gere & Goodno, Mechanics of Materials.
